project.purpose: Evolve the already-operational Runtime into a LEGO-centric physical-execution kernel by preserving proven behavior while extracting state, authority, provider, control, evidence, and compatibility seams; do not recreate a generic Execution Fabric.

nodes.label: RuntimeInvariantFreeze
nodes.responsibility: Freeze the externally observable laws that refactoring must preserve: Workspace lineage/source-state, Job/Attempt identity, replay, reservations, cancellation, terminal commit, Artifact identity, ambiguity, release, Tool catalog and error semantics.
acceptance: A machine-readable invariant manifest exists and every invariant maps to at least one current test or an explicitly added contract test.
The 23-tool public catalog, Tool schemas, Registry semantic version, and current release/rollback laws are frozen as refactor constraints unless a later slice explicitly changes them.
Execution Fabric R1 remains retired and is listed as a negative architecture constraint.
nodes.nextAction: Maintain the invariant manifest as a refactor fence; any deliberate public-law change must update its proofs explicitly.

nodes.label: ContractTestPartition
nodes.responsibility: Partition the current large tests into contract, property, provider, migration, recovery, and integration suites without changing behavior.
acceptance: Existing test count and assertions are preserved or strengthened.
Contract tests are runnable independently from provider/system acceptance.
No semantic behavior change is required to complete the split.
nodes.nextAction: Keep the independently runnable Tool Catalog and projection contract partitions as the baseline feedback gate; continue broader taxonomy-driven physical splits opportunistically without blocking noun-level state extraction.

nodes.label: WorkspaceStateModule
nodes.responsibility: Extract Workspace identity, source-state commitment, lifecycle CAS, dependency fence, and tombstone semantics from the historical engine aggregation.
acceptance: Workspace open/get/list/close behavior and replay remain byte-for-byte/schema compatible at the MCP boundary.
sourceRevision/currentHeadRevision/sourceStateDigest invariants remain unchanged.
Workspace lifecycle tests no longer require unrelated Job/Provider internals except through declared interfaces.
nodes.nextAction: The first WorkspaceState contract slice is integrated (projection plus mutation/close guards); extract additional Workspace laws only where duplicate semantics remain, without duplicating Git mechanics.

nodes.label: JobAttemptStateModule
nodes.responsibility: Extract logical Job identity and physical Attempt-generation lifecycle into explicit state modules.
evidence: R03-A1 candidate verification: owner-environment test PASS; extended reference-model 1/1 PASS; local-acceptance supervisor 2/2 + Runtime integration 36/36 + MCP/Workspace/Release E2E PASS

R03-A2 candidate verification: job_attempt_state 9/9; owner-environment test PASS; extended reference-model 1/1 PASS; local-acceptance supervisor 2/2 + Runtime integration 36/36 + MCP/Workspace/Release E2E PASS
acceptance: Job replay never redispatches an already committed operation.
Attempt generation and terminalization preserve current ambiguity/lost/orphaned behavior.
Physical provider code depends on Job/Attempt contracts rather than engine internals.
nodes.nextAction: R03 is closed at the planned A1/A2 seam and R04 ReservationContract is integrated on the verified candidate; proceed to R05 ArtifactAndReleaseStateModule without reopening Job/Attempt ownership.

nodes.label: ReservationStateModule
nodes.responsibility: Extract durable capacity reservation and one-active-execution-per-Workspace laws into an independently testable component.
evidence: owner verification on verified candidate 4131cbe02c54ea2ea419aeb80c651231c940ecf3:job-01a0cd18-695a-7dc3-b07a-a712d3bd2a31 PASS (exitCode=0; core 261/261 runnable PASS with 36 opt-in ignored; focused reference-model 1/1 PASS; MCP 66/66 PASS; auth 10/10 PASS; owner environment and documentation contract valid)

prior equivalent-R04-patch physical acceptance on an earlier base: fast-success race 1/1 PASS and timeout-descendant-pipes 1/1 PASS; clean baseline independently reproduced the launch-evidence race, so it is not owned by R04
integration equivalence: integrated e48b2eab5fb743efa3b50cb1eceae4539e1c99a7 is byte-identical to verified 4131cbe02c54ea2ea419aeb80c651231c940ecf3 across the five R04 responsibility files
acceptance: Global limit remains a strict durable invariant across restart.
Rejected admission remains commitState=not_started.
No queue, priority scheduler, or second in-memory capacity truth is introduced.
nodes.nextAction: R04 is closed. Proceed to R05 ArtifactAndReleaseStateModule; keep queue, priority, scheduling, and launch-evidence reconciliation outside ReservationContract.

nodes.label: ArtifactAndReleaseStateModule
nodes.responsibility: Separate Artifact/result identity and structured Runtime release effect state from generic engine/storage aggregation while preserving their distinct semantics.
nodes.authority: Runtime Artifact truth and Runtime self-release effect truth
evidence: core qualification job-01a0ce0a-9ceb-77d2-b9e0-ff7ba85b37e9 PASS: 269 runnable core tests PASS with 36 opt-in ignored; platform owner boundary 2/2 PASS

owner verification job-01a0ce0e-7915-78d2-9a79-fcdb8d324756 PASS: cargo fmt, owner environment, all-features clippy, transactional Runtime 292 PASS with 36 opt-in ignored, MCP 66/66 PASS, auth 10/10 PASS, extended reference-model 1/1 PASS, documentation contract valid; terminal-evidence sha256:384885d11bb3b43656fc722fc6e6a3f4cef70f0bdea7d0e0df0da82a16de5dba
Registry MAX_MIGRATION_VERSION remains 6; R05 introduces no SQL/schema migration and no public MCP Tool change
acceptance: Artifact reads remain digest-bound and Job/Attempt attributable.
release.apply/release.get remain the only graduated structured external effect in Runtime.
No generic EffectAdapter, effect registry, or caller-supplied effect class is introduced.
nodes.nextAction: R05 is closed. Proceed to R06 RegistryStorageBoundary; preserve Artifact/result and Runtime self-release as distinct operation-specific semantics and do not introduce a generic Effect framework.

nodes.label: RegistryStorageBoundary
nodes.responsibility: Reduce Registry to transactional persistence, migration, query, and reconstructible-index duties while state semantics remain owned by explicit state modules.
acceptance: Registry schema remains v6 unless an explicit semantic migration is proven necessary.
Performance-only indexes remain reconstructible and outside semantic migrations.
State modules can be unit-tested against a narrow transactional storage contract.
nodes.nextAction: Introduce narrow persistence interfaces only after state ownership is explicit.

nodes.label: AuthorityContract
nodes.responsibility: Compile execution target, profile, principal, input authority, credential authority, Windows authority, executable identity and Host Dependency commitments into one internal enforceable authority contract.
nodes.authority: Runtime authority binding; grants remain external/provider owned
acceptance: Existing exec/execBound/execBoundTrusted/execCredentialBoundTrusted requests compile to explicit AuthorityContract variants without widening any authority.
Runtime consumes and enforces authority; it does not invent provider/domain permission.
Replay resolves existing Jobs before current authority/policy reinterpretation exactly as today.
nodes.nextAction: Model current four execution families as internal authority compositions before changing any public Tool.

nodes.label: OperationCircuitCompiler
nodes.responsibility: Compile a typed request plus state, authority, inputs, budgets, provider commitment and evidence obligations into one immutable Execution Plan/circuit.
acceptance: All execution Tools map to the same compiler with explicit LEGO selections rather than bespoke admission paths.
Legacy all-explicit request identity remains replay-compatible.
Compiled plans contain only enforceable facts; metadata without enforcement does not enter operation identity.
nodes.nextAction: Introduce compiler output as an internal type and migrate one Tool path first behind compatibility tests.

nodes.label: ExecutionProviderSPI
nodes.responsibility: Define the minimal provider contract for validate, realize, observe, cancel and reconcile without turning Runtime into a provider marketplace.
acceptance: Local Linux and Windows Native can satisfy the same provider-level obligations without pretending their OS mechanisms are identical.
Provider replacement cannot strengthen caller assumptions or weaken process ownership, evidence, cancellation, or reconciliation guarantees.
No dynamic plugin registry is required for R1.
nodes.nextAction: Freeze assume/guarantee obligations before extracting either provider.

nodes.label: LocalLinuxProvider
nodes.responsibility: Move systemd/cgroup Runner realization, trusted/contained profiles, Linux continuity witnesses and cancellation/reconciliation behind the provider seam.
acceptance: trusted_local and contained_local retain current semantics and evidence scopes.
systemd/cgroup real-system acceptance passes for the exact candidate commit.
Host Dependency and executable path continuity claims retain runtime_host_namespace_path_witness limitations.
nodes.nextAction: Extract provider adapter without changing Runner wire contract.

nodes.label: WindowsNativeProvider
nodes.responsibility: Move SCM/Job Object launcher, token/ACL, Power Request, immutable-input realization and native reconstruction behind the provider seam.
acceptance: Native Windows remains WSL-independent.
limited/elevated ordinary execution and limited-only input-bound execution retain current admission rules.
Windows real-system acceptance passes before provider extraction is accepted.
nodes.nextAction: Extract Windows provider only after SPI obligations are proven with Linux.

nodes.label: ControlPrimitives
nodes.responsibility: Extract small reusable mechanical controls—fence, reservation, drain, revalidate, CAS, commit, rollback, quarantine, receipt—without creating a generic Effect engine.
acceptance: Release, Workspace close and lifecycle/cache paths can reuse primitives while preserving operation-specific state/evidence.
No second durable lifecycle is introduced alongside Job/Attempt unless a concrete owner proves it necessary.
Control primitives remain pure/mechanical enough to test independently.
nodes.nextAction: Start with Fence/Revalidate/CAS because they already recur across release and lifecycle operations.

nodes.label: EvidenceClaimModel
nodes.responsibility: Represent machine claims as subject + claim + scope + witness + observation + boundary + limitation while retaining historical evidence compatibility.
acceptance: Provider, executable, Host Dependency and terminal evidence can project through the model without losing current fields.
Every positive continuity claim names its exact scope and limitation.
Historical evidence remains readable; no migration is required merely to introduce the internal model.
nodes.nextAction: Map current evidence records into a claim matrix before changing serialization.

nodes.label: MCPRequestAdapter
nodes.responsibility: Keep the 23 public Tools strongly typed while making them thin request adapters into state/authority/compiler/control LEGO.
acceptance: Tool catalog digest is unchanged for structural-only waves.
Tools contain schema/adaptation logic, not duplicate admission or provider semantics.
Connector/client catalog refresh is required only when a deliberate public contract change occurs.
nodes.nextAction: Migrate one execution Tool end-to-end, then prove schema/catalog identity before the remaining Tools.

nodes.label: OperatorPlaneDecomposition
nodes.responsibility: Turn deploy/status/lifecycle/reclaim/cache scripts into thin operator compositions over stable Runtime control/state primitives where practical.
acceptance: Operator scripts shrink by moving proven shared mechanics into owner-local libraries, not by hiding behavior in a generic framework.
Release receipt and rollback compatibility remain exact.
Fast health stays bounded by active state rather than historical Registry size.
nodes.nextAction: Extract pure receipt/fence/status projection helpers first; leave CLI orchestration intact until parity is proven.

nodes.label: StabilityEnvelope
nodes.responsibility: Define the future 1.0 stability envelope: stable identity/lifecycle/error/evidence laws versus intentionally evolvable provider/profile extensions.
acceptance: Stable and evolvable surfaces are explicitly enumerated.
Deprecation/migration/rollback rules exist for Tool, Registry and evidence evolution.
A provider implementation can evolve without redefining Workspace/Job/Attempt semantics.
nodes.nextAction: Draft the envelope only after internal seams are proven; do not declare 1.0 early.

nodes.label: CrossPlaneFalsification
nodes.responsibility: Attack composition seams with real-system faults and ambiguity cases rather than accepting local unit correctness as whole-system correctness.
acceptance: Linux real-system acceptance binds exact candidate commit and binary digests.
Windows native acceptance proves process-tree ownership and reconstruction for provider changes.
Fault cases cover response loss, provider drift, path drift, cancellation races, crash/restart reconciliation, release rollback and Workspace close CAS.
No ambiguity case is converted into success or blind redispatch.
nodes.nextAction: Maintain a seam-specific falsification matrix and require exact evidence for each structural wave.

nodes.label: StructuralClosure
nodes.responsibility: Delete historical aggregation only after all new seams prove behavioral equivalence and reduce oversized engine/registry/operator ownership.
acceptance: engine.rs, registry.rs and MCP tools no longer contain materially different hidden authorities.
Old compatibility shims are deleted only with replay/migration evidence.
Source complexity decreases without adding a generic Fabric, effect framework or provider registry.
nodes.nextAction: Measure deleted responsibilities and code after each extraction; closure is deletion, not another abstraction layer.

edges.label: reservation belongs to admitted execution lifecycle
Workspace state owns semantics above storage
Job/Attempt state owns semantics above storage
admission binds Job to enforceable authority
control primitives commit through durable storage
Linux provider must survive real-system attacks
Windows provider must survive native attacks
operator composition must preserve release/lifecycle truth
only proven replacement permits old aggregation deletion

slices.objective: Freeze Runtime laws and split verification so structural work cannot silently change behavior.
acceptance: Invariant manifest complete.
Contract/property/provider/migration/integration tests independently addressable.
No public Tool or Registry semantic change.
slices.nextAction: R00 and the R01 baseline gate are complete; continue broader physical test partition opportunistically while RW1 state-contract extraction proceeds behind independently runnable contract and real-system gates.

slices.objective: Extract durable state ownership from historical engine/registry aggregation.
acceptance: Workspace/Job/Attempt/Reservation/Artifact/Release semantics each have explicit owner modules.
Registry is storage/transaction/migration rather than the semantic owner.
Registry schema remains v6 unless a separately reviewed semantic migration is unavoidable.
evidence: local-acceptance: supervisor 2/2 + Runtime integration 36/36 + MCP/Workspace/Release E2E PASS on 5bd241df24da3259c1c6e3637bf3fc513129e4b9
crates/ordivon-runtime-core/src/runtime/job_attempt_state.rs (R03-A1 canonical v3/v4/v5/v6 operation identity + exact replay/conflict law)
R04 ReservationContract: integrated e48b2eab, tree-equivalent to verified candidate 4131cbe0; full owner verification PASS; prior equivalent-patch focused real-system acceptance PASS
R05 ArtifactAndReleaseStateModule: commit 2954b576; full owner verification PASS; Registry v6/public MCP surface preserved; no generic Effect abstraction
slices.nextAction: R05 is complete. Proceed to R06 RegistryStorageBoundary; keep R02 open only for additional proven Workspace-law duplication.

slices.objective: Compile existing execution variants from orthogonal authority and operation LEGO instead of bespoke feature paths.
acceptance: Four current execution families compile through one internal operation compiler.
Replay/identity compatibility is preserved.
No generic public authority object is introduced.
slices.nextAction: Start with a matrix of current Tool→authority→provider→evidence composition, then implement one end-to-end migration.

slices.objective: Establish replaceable provider seams and move Linux/Windows OS mechanics behind them.
acceptance: Provider assume/guarantee contract is explicit.
Linux and Windows both satisfy it without sharing false OS equivalences.
Cross-node routing/provider marketplace remain outside Runtime.
slices.nextAction: Prove SPI with Linux first, then move Windows; do not implement a third provider without a real workload.

slices.objective: Extract reusable control and evidence LEGO without recreating generic Execution Fabric or Effect infrastructure.
acceptance: Fence/CAS/revalidate/receipt mechanics are independently testable.
Evidence claims carry scope and limitation.
Self-release remains operation-specific; opaque commands remain effect-opaque.
slices.nextAction: Extract the smallest recurring primitive first and reject any abstraction that requires a second durable lifecycle.

slices.objective: Thin MCP and operator surfaces over the extracted LEGO composition.
acceptance: 23 public Tools remain strongly typed.
Tool catalog digest stays stable for structural-only work.
Deploy/status/lifecycle/reclaim/cache lose duplicate mechanics rather than merely moving code.
slices.nextAction: Migrate one MCP execution Tool and one operator path, prove parity, then expand.

slices.objective: Prove whole-system substitutability and define the stable public evolution envelope.
acceptance: Linux and Windows real-system evidence covers changed seams.
All ambiguity/recovery invariants survive structural refactoring.
Stable versus evolvable contracts are explicit enough for a future 1.0 decision.
slices.nextAction: Run seam-specific falsification before declaring any extracted interface stable.

slices.objective: Delete obsolete aggregation and freeze the LEGO-centric architecture.
acceptance: Historical aggregation shrinks materially.
No duplicate state/control/effect framework remains.
Owner-native verification, extended property tests, real-system acceptance, root repo:ci and release/rollback proof are all green.
slices.nextAction: Delete only code whose replacement has current acceptance evidence.

gaps: Core state semantics are conceptually separated but still aggregated in large engine.rs/types.rs/registry.rs modules.
Execution authority dimensions exist but are composed partly through feature-specific Tool paths rather than one internal authority contract.
Linux and Windows share semantics but do not yet sit behind a minimal explicit provider SPI.
Mechanical control primitives recur across release/lifecycle/cache/Workspace operations but are not fully explicit reusable LEGO.
Evidence is strong but not yet represented through one internal claim/scope/witness/limitation model.
MCP and operator surfaces still contain some duplicated composition logic.
contained_local remains experimental within its declared reduced-authority boundary.
Windows Long Paths admission evidence remains unimplemented.
No current production need justifies hostile-code isolation, non-systemd Linux, macOS, remote scheduling, generic effects or a provider marketplace inside Runtime.

review.notes: RW0 baseline remains complete. R02 first WorkspaceState slice remains integrated; R03 Job/Attempt and R04 ReservationContract are complete. R05 now gives Artifact/result identity plus Runtime self-release request/binding/receipt interpretation an explicit owner-local module while preserving Registry v6, the public MCP Tool surface, digest-bound Artifact reads, and release.apply/release.get as the only graduated structured external effect. Full Runtime owner verification passed on the exact candidate. RW1 remains open: next frontier is R06 RegistryStorageBoundary.
